prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate objective function for a GNN-based netlist tier-partitioner (2-tier 3D IC).
Hypothesis of the change: The parent's `l_loc` double-counts criticality and its gradient keeps pulling critical pins apart because it is normalised per net (so a huge critical hub net dominates), and it lacks any direct pressure to keep critical pins on the same side; replacing it with a pairwise star-expansion term whose per-pin weight is a *saturating* criticality (crit, not crit^2) times a fan-out damping 1/log(1+k) applied to the *net*, and normalising by the total pin weight, will lower crit_cross without letting hub nets swamp small critical nets, shrinking TNS.
Rule-based digest (scores are improvement ratios vs. the official baseline; C1..C3 are the training circuits by size):
total=+0.075 robust(mean-std)=-0.019 min_case=-0.033 seed_std=0.054 tns_mean=+0.020 all_valid=True
  C1: score=+0.073 dWNS=+10.5% dTNS=+5.7% per-seed=[-0.02 +0.08 +0.17]
  C2: score=+0.035 dWNS=+7.8% dTNS=+0.8% per-seed=[+0.09 +0.01 +0.00]
  C3: score=-0.033 dWNS=-9.8% dTNS=+0.1% per-seed=[-0.02 -0.09 +0.01]
  partition stats vs baseline:
  C1: cut 137->134, wcut 421->394, crit_cross 0.011->0.016, repair_flips 103->121, changed-vs-baseline 15.7%
  C2: cut 318->308, wcut 1007->971, crit_cross 0.000->0.000, repair_flips 238->228, changed-vs-baseline 5.3%
  C3: cut 582->581, wcut 1955->1947, crit_cross 0.069->0.061, repair_flips 353->350, changed-vs-baseline 3.3%
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID, first classify the failure (crash / non-finite loss / balance repair failure / timeout) and whether it is systematic or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which circuit/metric moved and the plausible mechanism (cut nets, critical-pair cross-tier, repair flips)? (3) is the seed spread acceptable? (4) one concrete next step. No preamble.

response:
(1) Partially. TNS improved on C1/C2 but C3 regressed; crit_cross rose on C1 (0.011→0.016) despite the same-side pressure, so the saturating/damped weighting didn't reliably reduce critical crossings.

(2) C1: cut/wcut down, dWNS +10.5%, dTNS +5.7%, but crit_cross up and repair_flips up (103→121) — more repair churn likely from hub-net damping weakening critical-pin cohesion. C3: crit_cross down (0.069→0.061) yet dWNS −9.8%, suggesting cut reduction didn't translate to timing.

(3) Seed spread is high (std 0.054, min −0.033); not acceptable.

(4) Ablate the 1/log(1+k) damping vs crit-only weighting on C3 to isolate the regression.
